explanation: Its title comes from the French idiom faire les quatre cents coups, to raise hell. Truffaut followed his on-screen double, Antoine Doinel, through four more films over twenty years.

claims.text: François Truffaut directed The 400 Blows (1959), drawing on his own troubled childhood.
Truffaut was a film critic before he became a director.
Jean-Luc Godard, Claude Chabrol and Éric Rohmer did not direct Les Quatre Cents Coups.
The title The 400 Blows comes from the French idiom 'faire les quatre cents coups', meaning to raise hell.
Truffaut made four more films about Antoine Doinel, the hero of The 400 Blows, over the following twenty years.
